title: gEdit dialect profile
description: A dialect profile of gEdit: how one kind of NC program is written. A profile file with "extends" writes only what differs from the profile it builds on; a file without it writes everything. gEdit checks every profile itself when it loads it; this schema gives an editor the same help while you type.
$comment: Written by hand from src/lib/core/profiles/types.ts and held to validateProfile by src/lib/core/profiles/schema.test.ts. The rules JSON Schema cannot say are listed there (VALIDATOR_ONLY).

$schema.title: Schema
$schema.description: The address of this schema, so an editor such as VS Code can check the file while you type. gEdit does not read it.

id.title: Id
id.description: The name of the profile inside gEdit: small letters, digits, ".", "_" and "-", for example "shop-lathe". It is the file name of a profile of your own.

name.title: Name
name.description: The full name of the profile, shown in the profile list, at most 80 characters.

shortName.title: Short name
shortName.description: The name in the status bar, at most 16 characters, for example "FANUC".

version.title: Version
version.description: The version of this profile file, a whole number from 1. Raise it when you change the file.

extends.title: Builds on
extends.description: The id of the profile this one builds on, for example "fanuc-lathe". Everything you do not write here comes from it; a list you write replaces the whole list.

grammar.title: Colouring
grammar.description: Which colouring rules the editor uses: "iso" (Fanuc and similar), "klartext" (Heidenhain), "okuma" or "sinumerik".

codes.title: Code list
codes.description: The id of the code list this profile reads (G and M codes, cycles, templates), for example "fanuc-lathe".

files.title: Files
files.description: The file names of this kind of program and how new files are written.

extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.description: The file extensions of these programs without the dot, in small letters, the usual one first, for example ["nc", "tap"]. JSON and Python files cannot be NC programs.

defaultExtension.title: Default extension
defaultExtension.description: The extension a new file gets. It has to be one of the extensions.

filterName.title: File type name
filterName.description: The name of these files in the open and save dialogs, for example "Fanuc programs".

encoding.title: Encoding
encoding.description: Always "keep": a file is saved in the encoding it was opened with.

lineEnding.title: Line ending
lineEnding.description: Always "keep": a file keeps the line endings it was opened with.

newFileLineEnding.title: Line ending of a new file

detect.title: Detection
detect.description: How gEdit tells that a file is one of these programs when it is opened.

extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.description: File extensions in small letters without the dot, and how much each one counts, for example { "nc": 1, "mpf": 10 }.

content.title: Content
content.description: Patterns tested on the first lines of the file, each with a weight. On each line only the strongest matching pattern counts.

folders.title: Folders
folders.description: A file inside one of these folders uses this profile outright, for example "/programs/lathe".

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Decides between two profiles that score the same; the higher one wins.

vetoes.title: Not this kind of program
vetoes.description: Patterns that rule this profile out: when one matches any line read, the profile scores nothing for the file, for example "DIAMON" on a milling profile.

syntax.title: Syntax
syntax.description: How the text of a program is written: comments, block numbers, decimal points and the special words of the control.

caseSensitive.title: Case sensitive
caseSensitive.description: True: patterns and codes match small and capital letters apart. Left out: they match either.

strings.title: Strings
strings.description: True when " opens a text string, as in Heidenhain tool names. Left out: a quote is an ordinary character.

comments.title: Comments
comments.description: How a comment starts and ends, for example { "start": "(", "end": ")" } or { "start": ";", "end": null } for a comment that runs to the end of the line.

start.title: Start
start.description: The text that opens the comment, for example "(" or ";".

end.title: End
end.description: The text that closes it, for example ")", or null when the comment runs to the end of the line.

sectionHeading.title: Section heading
sectionHeading.description: A line that matches this starts a section in the program map.

continuation.title: Line continues
continuation.description: Matches the mark at the end of a line that joins it to the next line, for example "~$" on Heidenhain.

continuationMark.title: Continuation mark
continuationMark.description: The mark itself, used where gEdit writes one, for example "~".

continuationStart.title: Line belongs to the block above
continuationStart.description: Matches the mark at the start of a line that belongs to the block above it, for example "^\$ " on Okuma. It has to start with ^ in every alternative and may not match a line without the mark.

blockSkip.title: Block skip
blockSkip.description: The block skip mark, for example "/".

chars.title: Marks
chars.description: The characters that skip a block, for example "/".

levels.title: Levels
levels.description: True when a digit after the mark selects a skip level, for example /2.

plainLevel.title: Level of a plain mark
plainLevel.description: The level a mark without a digit is: "0" on Siemens, "1" on Fanuc.

blockNumber.title: Block numbers
blockNumber.description: How a block number is written.

mode.title: Kind
mode.description: "prefix": a letter and a number, for example N10. "leading-integer": a plain number at the start of the line, as on Heidenhain.

prefix.title: Letter
prefix.description: The letter of a block number, usually "N". Needed when the kind is "prefix".

altPrefixes.title: Other letters
altPrefixes.description: Other letters that also start a block number; renumbering writes the main letter instead.

mandatory.title: Required
mandatory.description: True when every block has to have a block number.

mainPrefix.title: Main block mark
mainPrefix.description: The mark of a main block number, one character that is no letter, digit or blank, for example ":" on Siemens (:123). It may not be a character that already starts a comment, a block skip, a string, a sign or an expression.

decimalSeparator.title: Decimal separator
decimalSeparator.description: The character that starts the fraction of a number: "." or ",".

decimalSeparatorAlt.title: Second decimal separator
decimalSeparatorAlt.description: A second character also read as a decimal separator, for example "," beside "." on Heidenhain. New numbers are still written with the first one.

decimalPointSignificant.title: Decimal point matters
decimalPointSignificant.description: True when X10 and X10. mean different values (a number without a point counts in increments). It has to agree with the default number input of the machine settings.

wordSeparatorRequired.title: Blanks between words
wordSeparatorRequired.description: True when words have to be separated by blanks (Heidenhain); false when words may be packed, as in N10G1X10.

incrementalPrefix.title: Incremental mark
incrementalPrefix.description: The letter in front of an axis word that makes it incremental, for example "I" in IX10 on Heidenhain.

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Matches a variable, for example "#\d+" or "R\d+". It has to take at least one character.

keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.description: Words of the control that are read before single letters, for example "GOTO" or "TOOL CALL".

maxLineLength.title: Longest block
maxLineLength.description: The most characters a block may have on this control.

maxWordDigits.title: Most digits in a word
maxWordDigits.description: The most digits a word may have once the control counts it in increments, for example 8 on Fanuc. Check Program reports a longer one.

maxMCodes.title: Most M codes in a block
maxMCodes.description: The most M codes the control takes in one block, for example 8 on Okuma.

sequenceNames.title: Block names
sequenceNames.description: True when a block number letter may also carry a name, for example NLAP1 on Okuma. Such a name is never renumbered.

assignment.title: Assignment words
assignment.description: Matches a word written with "=" and a value, for example "SB=1200" on Okuma or "CR=15" on Siemens.

labels.title: Labels
labels.description: Matches a label at the start of a block, for example "LOOP_A:" on Siemens. It has to name the label with the group (?<name>…).

calls.title: Calls with brackets
calls.description: True when a name written in front of "(" is a call with its arguments, for example CYCLE81(10,0,2,-12) on Siemens.

systemVariables.title: System variables
systemVariables.description: Matches a variable of the control itself, for example "\$[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*" on Siemens.

systemVariableNumbers.title: First system variable number
systemVariableNumbers.description: The number from which on a numbered variable belongs to the control, for example 1000 on Fanuc (#5221 is the X of G54). The geometry scripts refuse to change such a variable.

incrementTravelsShift.title: Increments travel a shift
incrementTravelsShift.description: True when an incremental move after a change of the zero point also travels that change, until the axis is written absolutely. Rotate and Mirror then refuse such a move.

tcpTableCoordinates.title: Tool centre point in table coordinates
tcpTableCoordinates.description: True when Translate should say that it reads tool centre point coordinates in the table's coordinate system, which a machine parameter may change.

cycleRAbsoluteWith.title: Cycle R absolute with
cycleRAbsoluteWith.description: The "Feeds without a point" choices under which the R of a drilling cycle can be an absolute position. Translate then adds a note where it leaves such an R as written.

extraAxisNames.title: Extra axis names
extraAxisNames.description: Axis names of more than one letter that the machine builder set up, such as AA (usually set on the machine page, not here). A Siemens control writes them with an equals sign (AA=90); some machines also take AA90. gEdit then reads both as a move of that axis, and Translate, Rotate and Mirror leave that axis as written. On a standard Siemens control AA90 alone is the name of a program, so list a name only if your machine reads it as an axis.

header.title: File header
header.description: Matches a header on the first line of the file, for example "^%_N_\w+_(MPF|SPF)" on Siemens.

names.title: Names
names.description: Matches a name the program gives itself, a variable or a jump target, so it is not read as a row of single letter words, for example "[A-Z_]{2}[A-Z0-9_]*".

programNames.title: Program names
programNames.description: Matches a program name written instead of a number, for example "<[A-Za-z0-9+\-_.]+>" on Fanuc. It has to take at least one character.

assignmentIndex.title: Indexed assignment
assignmentIndex.description: True when an assignment word may carry one index in brackets, for example LIMS[2]=1800 on Siemens.

extendedAddresses.title: Control addresses
extendedAddresses.description: Matches the assignment words that are addresses of the control, for example SB or TL on Okuma; the others are local variables.

exponentMarker.title: Exponent mark
exponentMarker.description: The letters of an exponent inside a number, at least two, for example "EX" in 1.5EX3 on Siemens.

symbolAddresses.title: Symbol addresses
symbolAddresses.description: Single characters that are the address of the value right behind them, for example "#" in #5 on Heidenhain. No letter, digit, blank, sign, bracket or a mark the profile already uses.

removeSpaces.title: Remove Spaces
removeSpaces.description: "refuse": the command is not offered (Siemens). "keepAroundLongAddresses": the blank beside a word with a longer address stays (Okuma).

freeText.title: Kept text
freeText.description: Patterns for text the control keeps but does not run, each with the group (?<text>…), for example the cycle name behind CYCL DEF on Heidenhain.

colonWords.title: Words with a colon
colonWords.description: Longer addresses whose value stands behind a colon, for example "VCONST" in VCONST:ON on Heidenhain.

callTargets.title: Called program names
callTargets.description: A program name written behind a call keyword, for example CALL OABCD on Okuma.

after.title: Behind
after.description: The keywords the name follows; each one has to be one of the keywords.

labelAfter.title: Jump keywords
labelAfter.description: Keywords behind which a name is a jump target, for example GOTOF on Siemens. Each one has to be one of the keywords.

declareAfter.title: Declaration keywords
declareAfter.description: Keywords that declare variables, for example DEF on Siemens. Each one has to be one of the keywords.

plainTextRun.title: Plain text run
plainTextRun.description: A run of this many letters or more without a digit is read as plain text, not as single letter words, for example 3 on Fanuc. At least 2.

tapeMarker.title: Tape mark
tapeMarker.description: False when a lone "%" is not a tape mark on this control (Heidenhain). Left out: it is.

addresses.title: Addresses
addresses.description: The letters of the axes and of the tool, feed and spindle words.

toolCall.title: Tool change
toolCall.description: How a tool change line looks and where its tool number is.

program.title: Program start and end
program.description: The lines that start and end a program in the file.

start.title: Program start
start.description: Patterns of a line that starts a program, for example "^O\d+" on Fanuc.

end.title: Program end
end.description: Patterns of a line that ends a program, for example "(?<![A-Z])M30(?!\d)".

endRecord.title: End line closes the file
endRecord.description: True when the end line closes the program in the file and is not a block the program could skip, for example END PGM on Heidenhain.

outline.title: Program map
outline.description: The rules that build the program map, in order: the first rule that matches a line decides. Each names a kind (tool, program, section, comment, label, stop, end, subprogram-call) and a pattern; the groups (?<text>…) and (?<name>…) give the label.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What the line is in the program map.

pattern.title: Pattern
pattern.description: A line that matches this gets a row of that kind.

numbering.title: Block numbers
numbering.description: How Renumber, automatic block numbers and Go to Block number the blocks.

numberFormat.title: Number format
numberFormat.description: How the transforms write a number they change.

decimals.title: Decimals
decimals.description: "keep": as many decimals as written. A number from 0 to 9: round to that many decimals (half away from zero).

trailingZeros.title: Trailing zeros
trailingZeros.description: "keep" or "drop" the zeros at the end of the fraction.

keepPoint.title: Keep the point
keepPoint.description: True: a number whose fraction is dropped keeps its decimal point (10. stays 10.).

plusSign.title: Plus sign
plusSign.description: "keep" as written, "always", "never", or "signed": a + where the written number had a sign of either kind.

modal.title: Power-on state
modal.description: The codes in force when the control is switched on. Units and diameter programming are the machine's settings and cannot be written here.

initial.title: Power-on codes
initial.description: Modal group and the code in force at the start of a program, written as the code list writes it, for example { "motion": "G0", "plane": "G17" } ("G0", not "G00").

machineParams.title: Machine settings
machineParams.description: What a machine of this profile may set on the machine page, with the documented defaults. Left out: the profile has no machine settings.

onLoad.title: When a file is opened
onLoad.description: What gEdit does to a file of this profile when it opens it.

stripNul.title: Remove NUL characters
stripNul.description: True: NUL characters at the start and end of the file (tape leader) are removed.

toolList.title: Tool list
toolList.description: How the tool list finds the description of a tool.

description.title: Description
description.description: Where the comment that describes a tool stands: "auto" (tries the others), "above", "below" or "trailing" (on the same line).

commentFilter.title: Decoration
commentFilter.description: A comment that matches this is decoration, for example a row of dashes, and not a description.

dropLeadingZeros.title: Drop leading zeros
dropLeadingZeros.description: True: T01 is listed as tool 1.

collapseOffsetDigits.title: Tool and offset as one
collapseOffsetDigits.description: True: a lathe tool word with its offset digits (T0101) is listed as one tool.

compare.title: Compare
compare.description: What Compare ignores by default for programs of this profile.

ignoreBlockNumbers.title: Ignore block numbers
ignoreBlockNumbers.description: True: block numbers are left out of the comparison.

ignoreWhitespace.title: Ignore blanks
ignoreWhitespace.description: True: blanks are left out of the comparison.

ignoreComments.title: Ignore comments
ignoreComments.description: True: comments are left out, except the ones the control reads (see "Comments the control reads").

ignoreCase.title: Ignore case
ignoreCase.description: True: small and capital letters compare alike.

ignoreNumberFormat.title: Ignore number format
ignoreNumberFormat.description: True: X10.0 and X10. compare alike where they mean the same value.

ignoreCycleNames.title: Ignore cycle names
ignoreCycleNames.description: True: the cycle names in dialog language are left out. Offered only with cycle name patterns.

keepComments.title: Comments the control reads
keepComments.description: A line that matches one of these patterns keeps its comments when comments are ignored.

cycleNames.title: Cycle names
cycleNames.description: Patterns that find the cycle names in dialog language, each with the group (?<name>…).

tolerance.title: Tolerance (not used)
tolerance.description: Kept from older files and not read.

editing.title: Typing
editing.description: How typing behaves in a program of this profile.

forceUppercase.title: Capital letters
forceUppercase.description: True: letters typed outside comments and strings are written as capitals.

preventLineJoin.title: Keep lines apart
preventLineJoin.description: True: Backspace at the start and Delete at the end of a line do not join two blocks.

autoSpace.title: Blank between words
autoSpace.description: True: a blank is put in front of a new address word typed right after a word, so G1X becomes G1 X.

autoNumber.title: Next block number
autoNumber.description: True: Enter at the end of a numbered block starts the next line with the next block number.

tabWidth.title: Tab width
tabWidth.description: How many columns a tab takes in programs of this profile, 1 to 16. Left out: the general setting.

rulers.title: Rulers
rulers.description: Columns where a ruler line is drawn, at most 8, each from 1 to 1000, for example [80]. An empty list shows none. Left out: the general setting.

colors.title: Code colours
colors.description: Colours of this profile's programs, per theme, written as #rrggbb, for example { "dark": { "feed": "#ffaa00" } }. Each colour has to be readable on the editor background (a contrast of at least 4.5 to 1). Left out: your own code colours, then the built-in ones.

dark.title: Dark theme
dark.description: The colour of each kind of word in the dark theme.

light.title: Light theme
light.description: The colour of each kind of word in the light theme.

pattern.title: Pattern
pattern.description: A regular expression tested against each line, for example "^%" or "(?<![A-Z])G96(?!\d)".

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: How much one match counts. A larger weight makes this rule more decisive than the others.

trigger.title: Tool change line
trigger.description: A line that matches this changes the tool, for example "(?<![A-Z])M0?6(?!\d)" for M6 or "TOOL CALL" on Heidenhain.

tool.title: Tool number
tool.description: Finds the tool number on a line. It has to name the number with the group (?<tool>…), for example "(?<![A-Z])T(?<tool>\d+)".

toolFrom.title: Where the tool number is
toolFrom.description: "same-line": the T word on the tool change line. "same-line-or-last": that T word, or the last T written before the line. "last-before": the last T written before the line; a T on the change line itself selects the next tool.

ignore.title: Not a tool change
ignore.description: A tool change line that also matches this is not a tool change, for example a lathe line "T0100" that only cancels the offset.

tool.title: Tool address
tool.description: The letter of the tool word, usually "T".

feed.title: Feed address
feed.description: The letter of the feed word, usually "F".

rapid.title: Rapid word
rapid.description: The address or keyword that marks a rapid move where the control has one, for example "FMAX" on Heidenhain.

spindle.title: Spindle address
spindle.description: The letter of the spindle speed word, usually "S".

axes.title: Axes
axes.description: The axis addresses of this control, for example X, Y, Z, A, B, C. Lists at least one.

arcCenter.title: Arc centre words
arcCenter.description: The addresses that give the centre of an arc, for example I, J, K.

arcCenterMode.title: Arc centre values
arcCenterMode.description: "incremental": the centre is measured from the start point of the arc. "absolute": the centre is a position in the work coordinates.

incremental.title: Incremental addresses
incremental.description: An address that moves an axis by a distance, and the axis it moves, for example U moves X and W moves Z on a lathe. The axis has to be one of the axes.

diameter.title: Diameter addresses
diameter.description: The addresses written as a diameter while diameter programming is on, for example X and U on a lathe.

angular.title: Rotary axes
angular.description: The axes that turn, whose values are angles in degrees, for example A, B, C.

feedUnitWords.title: Feed unit words
feedUnitWords.description: Words that set the feed unit by themselves, for example FU for feed per revolution and FZ for feed per tooth on Heidenhain. Values: "per-minute", "per-rev", "per-tooth", "inverse-time".

speedLimitWords.title: Speed limit words
speedLimitWords.description: Words whose value limits the spindle speed instead of setting it, for example LIMS on Siemens. Scripts that scale speeds leave them alone.

offsetWords.title: Offset number words
offsetWords.description: Words that select an offset by its number and are never a position, for example D on Siemens. The geometry scripts leave them as written.

mainSpindle.title: Main spindle number
mainSpindle.description: The number of the main spindle where spindles are numbered, for example "1" on Siemens (S1= is then the main spindle).

arcDirectionWords.title: Arc direction words
arcDirectionWords.description: Where the arc direction is a word and not a G code: the word as written (an address and its sign) and the direction, for example "DR+" is "ccw" and "DR-" is "cw" on Heidenhain. At most one word per direction.

trigger.title: Line
trigger.description: A line that matches this carries a block number reference, for example "(?<![A-Z])M99(?!\d)".

addresses.title: Words
addresses.description: The words on that line whose value is a block number, for example P.

rewrite.title: Rewrite
rewrite.description: True (the default): renumbering writes the new number into the word. False: the reference is only reported, for example an M99 P that may name a block in the calling program.

program.title: Which program
program.description: "own" (the default): a block of the program the line stands in. "called": a block of the program the same line calls. "caller": a block of the program that called this one.

trigger.title: Line
trigger.description: A line that matches this calls another program, for example "(?<![A-Z])M98(?!\d)".

address.title: Program word
address.description: The word that names the called program, for example P in "M98 P1000".

maxDigits.title: Digits of the program number
maxDigits.description: The most digits the program number has. A longer value is a repeat count followed by the program number (Fanuc "M98 P21010" runs O1010 twice). Leave it out when the whole value is the program number.

repeatAddress.title: Repeat word
repeatAddress.description: The word that carries the repeat count instead, for example L. On a line with it, the whole value is the program number.

localAddress.title: Local call word
localAddress.description: The word that makes the line a call of a part of this same program when there is no program word, for example Q in "M98 Q30".

interrupt.title: Interrupt
interrupt.description: True when the line starts a program that runs on a signal and returns to whatever it interrupted, for example M96 P… on Fanuc.

external.title: Program on an external device
external.description: True when the line runs a program from an external device or a data server, not a program of the open file, for example M198 P… on Fanuc. A program of the same number in the file is not what a block word on that line names, so Renumber and Update References do not follow the call into it. The call still counts as a caller for the returns (M99) of that program.

mode.title: Numbering kind
mode.description: "free": any start and step. "consecutive": every block, step 1, no gaps (Heidenhain).

start.title: Start
start.description: The first block number, for example 10.

step.title: Step
step.description: The increment between block numbers, for example 10.

digits.title: Digits
digits.description: Pads the number with zeros to this many digits, for example 4 gives N0010. 0 or left out: no padding.

max.title: Largest number
max.description: The largest block number the control accepts, for example 99999.

onOverflow.title: Past the largest number
onOverflow.description: "wrap": start again at the start value. "stop": refuse to renumber.

spacesAfter.title: Blanks after the number
spacesAfter.description: How many blanks follow a new block number, 0 to 16.

skipStartingWith.title: Lines left unnumbered
skipStartingWith.description: Lines that start with one of these texts keep their text and get no number, for example "%" or "O".

skipEmpty.title: Skip empty lines
skipEmpty.description: True: empty lines get no number.

restartAtProgramStart.title: Restart at each program
restartAtProgramStart.description: True: numbering starts again at the start value at each program start in the file.

onlyNumbered.title: Only numbered blocks
onlyNumbered.description: True: only lines that already have a block number are renumbered.

fitToMax.title: Fit below the largest number
fitToMax.description: True: choose the largest whole step that keeps the last block at or below the largest number; the step is then not used. Needs a largest number.

alignColumn.title: Code column
alignColumn.description: The column (counted from 1) where the code behind a new block number starts. 0 or left out: the blanks after the number decide.

everyNth.title: Number every Nth block
everyNth.description: Numbers every Nth block; the blocks between lose their number, except a block that a jump or call names. 1 or left out: every block.

skipContaining.title: Lines containing
skipContaining.description: Lines that contain one of these texts keep their text unnumbered. Each text is one word without blanks.

skipFirst.title: Leave the first lines
skipFirst.description: The first this many lines are left as they are.

skipLast.title: Leave the last lines
skipLast.description: The last this many lines are left as they are.

startTrigger.title: Start at the text
startTrigger.description: Numbering starts at the first line that contains this text; the lines above keep their text. Empty: from the first line.

startAfterTrigger.title: Start after the text
startAfterTrigger.description: True: numbering starts at the line after the one with the start text.

references.title: Block number references
references.description: Lines whose words name a block number, so a renumber can follow them, for example M99 P30 or GOTO 100.

calls.title: Program calls
calls.description: Lines that call another program and the word that names it, for example M98 P1000. Read only to find the program a reference points into.

modal.title: Power-on state
modal.description: The power-on codes this choice sets, by modal group, for example { "initial": { "feedmode": "G99" } }.

initial.title: Power-on codes
initial.description: Modal group and the code in force when the control is switched on, written as the code list writes it ("G99", not "G099").

toolCall.title: Tool change
toolCall.description: How a tool change is read with this choice; the members you leave out stay as the profile says.

numbering.title: Block numbers
numbering.description: How blocks are numbered with this choice; the members you leave out stay as the profile says.

addresses.title: Addresses
addresses.description: The addresses with this choice, for example the incremental words of a lathe; the members you leave out stay as the profile says.

value.title: Value
value.description: The value stored on a machine, for example "A".

label.title: Label
label.description: What the machine page shows, for example "G-code system A".

codes.title: Code list
codes.description: The code list this choice reads, a code list that builds on the profile's own. Left out: the profile's code list.

overlay.title: Changes
overlay.description: What this choice changes in the profile: only the power-on state, the tool change, the block numbers and the addresses.

detect.title: Detection
detect.description: Patterns that point to this choice when a program has no machine. Each pattern counts its weight once.

id.title: Name
id.description: The name of the setting as a machine stores it, letters and digits, for example "gcodeSystem".

label.title: Label
label.description: What the machine page shows, for example "G-code system".

default.title: Default
default.description: The value of the choice that applies when nothing is chosen and nothing detected.

defaultBy.title: Default follows
defaultBy.description: Makes the default follow another setting of this profile: while that setting has one of the values listed, the default is the choice given for it.

variant.title: Other setting
variant.description: The name of the other setting, for example "gcodeSystem".

values.title: Defaults
values.description: A value of the other setting and the default it gives this one, for example { "B": "none" }.

choices.title: Choices
choices.description: The values a machine may choose from.

numberInput.title: Number input
numberInput.description: How a control may read the numbers of a program, offered by name on the machine page. Left out: numbers are read as the profile says, with no choice.

default.title: Default
default.description: The id of the choice that applies with no machine. It has to match the decimal point setting of the syntax.

presets.title: Choices
presets.description: The ways of reading numbers a machine may choose from.

id.title: Id
id.description: The name a machine stores, small letters, digits and "-", for example "is-b".

label.title: Label
label.description: What the machine page shows, for example "Increments of 0.001 mm (IS-B)". It says what the control does to a number.

value.title: Number reading
value.description: How numbers are read with this choice: the reading and the increments per kind of number.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the manual or the notes say so, for example the manual and its page. Shown beside the choice.

verify.title: Check on the machine
verify.description: True when the value is a documented default nobody has confirmed for a real machine yet; the choice is then marked as unconfirmed.

digitCheck.title: Counts for the digit check
digitCheck.description: False: the digit check of Check Program leaves this choice out when no machine is chosen, for example a coarse increment few machines run.

pointlessFeeds.title: Feeds without a point
pointlessFeeds.description: A machine option on top of the number input: how the control counts a feed written without a decimal point.

default.title: Default
default.description: The choice a machine has until it says otherwise. It sets no steps.

choices.title: Choices
choices.description: The ways a control may count a feed written without a decimal point.

value.title: Value
value.description: The value stored on a machine, for example "per-minute".

classes.title: Steps
classes.description: The step a feed without a point counts in, per kind of feed: "feedPerMin" and "feedPerRev". Each gives "increment" in mm and may give "incrementInch".

increment.title: Step (mm)
increment.description: The value of one step in a metric program, written as text, for example "0.001".

incrementInch.title: Step (inch)
incrementInch.description: The value of one step in an inch program, written as text, for example "0.00001".

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the manual or the notes say so, for example the manual and its page. Shown beside the choice.

verify.title: Check on the machine
verify.description: True when the value is a documented default nobody has confirmed for a real machine yet; the choice is then marked as unconfirmed.

units.title: Units
units.description: The units a machine starts in when nothing else is said: "mm" or "inch". Left out: mm.

diameter.title: Diameter programming
diameter.description: Lathes only: whether X is a diameter when the machine starts, "on" or "off".

modalGroups.title: Power-on codes
modalGroups.description: The modal groups of the code list whose power-on code a machine may set, for example "feedmode".

variants.title: Settings
variants.description: Settings with a fixed set of choices, for example the G-code system A or B of a lathe.

channels.title: Channels
channels.description: Starting points for a machine with more than one channel. They are never applied without a machine.

waitLetters.title: Wait code letters
waitLetters.description: The letters the wait codes of this control may use, one capital letter each, for example ["M"].

presets.title: Starting points
presets.description: The channel set-ups a machine may start from.

id.title: Id
id.description: The name of the starting point, small letters, digits and "-", for example "two-turrets".

value.title: Channels
value.description: The channels, their names and how they wait for each other.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the manual or the notes say so, for example the manual and its page. Shown beside the choice.

verify.title: Check on the machine
verify.description: True when the value is a documented default nobody has confirmed for a real machine yet; the choice is then marked as unconfirmed.

extraAxes.title: Extra axes
extraAxes.description: A machine of this profile may name extra axes, axis names of more than one letter that the machine builder set up (for example AA). Left out: the machine page does not offer them.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the manual or the notes say so, for example the manual and its page. Shown beside the choice.

verify.title: Check on the machine
verify.description: True when the value is a documented default nobody has confirmed for a real machine yet; the choice is then marked as unconfirmed.

builderCodes.title: Machine builder codes
builderCodes.description: A machine of this profile may list the machine builder's own codes, for example G810 to G829 on Siemens. Left out: the machine page does not offer them.

letters.title: Letters
letters.description: The letters such a code may have, one capital letter each, for example ["G"].

example.title: Example
example.description: Shown as the example of the field, for example "G810-G829".

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the manual or the notes say so, for example the manual and its page. Shown beside the choice.

verify.title: Check on the machine
verify.description: True when the value is a documented default nobody has confirmed for a real machine yet; the choice is then marked as unconfirmed.

presetNumberInput.$comment: Laid over machines.schema.json#/$defs/numberInput for a profile's preset: the validator holds a preset's increments to 1 or a power of ten below it, which a machine's own number input need not be.

incrementMm.title: Increment in mm
incrementMm.description: The smallest step of a length in a metric program, in mm, as 1 or a power of ten below it, for example "0.001".

incrementInch.title: Increment in inch
incrementInch.description: The same for an inch program, in inch, as 1 or a power of ten below it, for example "0.0001".

incrementDeg.title: Increment in degrees
incrementDeg.description: The smallest step of an angle, in degrees, as 1 or a power of ten below it.

incrementSec.title: Increment in seconds
incrementSec.description: The smallest step of a dwell time, in seconds, as 1 or a power of ten below it.

classes.title: Other kinds of number
classes.description: Where the control reads a kind of number differently from lengths. The increment of each is 1 or a power of ten below it.

increment.title: Increment
increment.description: The increment of this kind of number, as 1 or a power of ten below it, for example "0.001".

incrementInch.title: Increment in inch programs
incrementInch.description: The increment in an inch program, as 1 or a power of ten below it.
